goal: Build a travel-planning workflow. Given origin, destination, dates, budget and preferences, it should search flights and hotels, propose a complete itinerary within the budget, and ask the user for approval before anything is booked. It must never invent prices or availability that the search tools did not return, must clearly say when no option fits the budget, and must return a day-by-day plan with the total cost.

design.summary: Plan a trip from an origin to a destination using user-provided dates, budget, and preferences by searching flights and hotels, assembling a complete day-by-day itinerary within budget when possible, and requesting user approval before any booking occurs.
assumptions: The user will provide origin, destination, travel dates, budget, and preferences before planning begins.
Flight and hotel search systems can return current prices and availability.
The workflow can present an itinerary and total cost without making any bookings until the user approves.
If no combination fits the budget, the workflow can clearly report that no valid option was found and stop short of booking.
The workflow does not need to handle complex visa, passport, or insurance requirements unless explicitly requested.
successCriteria: Flights and hotels are searched using available lookup systems.
The workflow produces a day-by-day itinerary covering the full trip dates.
The workflow includes only prices and availability returned by the search tools and does not invent missing facts.
The total cost is calculated and shown to the user.
If no option fits the budget, the workflow clearly says so.
The workflow asks for user approval before any booking or reservation action is taken.
constraints: Must not invent prices or availability not returned by search tools.
Must not book anything without explicit user approval.
Must clearly indicate when no itinerary fits the budget.
Must provide a complete day-by-day plan with total cost.
Outputs should rely on current lookup data only.
